questions.question: What is Apollo Client? Explain the cache and fetch policies.
questions.title: Apollo Client Basics — InMemoryCache & Fetch Policies
questions.direct_answer:
What is Apollo Client? Explain the cache and fetch policies.

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser, network, and server contract (headers, cookies, streams)), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** useQuery, useMutation, InMemoryCache with normalized entities, fetch policies (cache-first, network-only, cache-and-network).

**Classic weak answer:** Using cache-first and wondering why the list doesn't reflect a new item — missing cache update logic on mutation.

**Senior finish:** Compare Apollo with urql and Relay; mention GraphQL Code Generator for typed hooks.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **Apollo Client Basics — InMemoryCache & Fetch Policies** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** What is Apollo Client? Explain the cache and fetch policies.

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **useQuery, useMutation, InMemoryCache with normalized entities, fetch policies (cache-first, network-only, cache-and-network)**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Using cache-first and wondering why the list doesn't reflect a new item — missing cache update logic on mutation**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Compare Apollo with urql and Relay; mention GraphQL Code Generator for typed hooks**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** useQuery, useMutation, InMemoryCache with normalized entities, fetch policies (cache-first, network-only, cache-and-network)
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

```mermaid
    API[(REST / GraphQL API)]
    UI --> CF --> IC --> CORS
    IC --> RETRY
    CF --> AC
    CORS --> API
    CACHE --> API
    RETRY --> API
```

sections.content:

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **using cache-first and wondering why the list doesn't reflect a new item — missing cache update logic on mutation** and what you do instead.

questions.question: Apollo vs urql vs Relay — which GraphQL client should you pick?
questions.title: Apollo vs urql vs Relay (2026) — GraphQL Client Comparison
questions.direct_answer:
Apollo vs urql vs Relay — which GraphQL client should you pick?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser, network, and server contract (headers, cookies, streams)), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Apollo: mature, feature-rich, big; urql: small, modular, exchanges; Relay: Meta-scale, opinionated, compiler-based.

**Classic weak answer:** Picking Relay without an existing compiler/fragment culture — its strengths come with a steep ramp.

**Senior finish:** Give 2026 recommendations: Apollo for most apps, urql for perf-sensitive frontends, Relay for massive Meta-scale codebases.
